title: CSAT Hard Revision Folder 2: Number systems, arithmetic, rates, geometry and table-based data interpretation

rubric.reasoning_layers: At least two linked deductions, constraints or conditional checks in every non-trivial item.
rubric.distractor_quality: All four options are plausible, distinct and comparable in visible length and specificity.
rubric.time_pressure: Complete paper: 80 questions in 120 minutes; revision drill: 40 questions in 75 minutes.
rubric.coverage: Comprehension, numeracy/DI, logical-analytical reasoning and decision-making are balanced.
rubric.verification: Every keyed answer is recomputed or independently constraint-checked before PDF generation.

questions.text: Which interpretation most accurately states the main proposition of Passage 1? Use the hostel attendance sheet as the complete information set for this question.
options: That technology adoption in small enterprises requires aligned incentives, evidence and local feedback rather than one universal prescription.
That technology adoption in small enterprises should be left to spontaneous private action without accountable public oversight.
That technology adoption in small enterprises can be solved through one nationwide institutional reform under all conditions.
That technology adoption in small enterprises is mainly technical and therefore has no significant distributive consequences.
questions.solution: The passage links the issue to incentives, evidence and feedback; the alternatives are absolute or narrowly framed.

questions.text: Which conclusion follows most securely from Passage 1? Use the river-route log as the complete information set for this question.
options: An intervention may fail despite a desirable objective when its feedback loop remains weak.
Administrative discretion is always harmful, even when evidence reveals local constraints.
A locally successful intervention will work identically elsewhere without any adaptation or review.
Measurement adds little when an intervention has a persuasive and desirable objective.
questions.solution: The passage distinguishes a desirable objective from the quality of its feedback loop; it rejects universal claims.

questions.text: Which presupposition is required by the argument in Passage 1? Use the border-connectivity map as the complete information set for this question.
options: Every measurable outcome is morally decisive regardless of the chosen public objective.
Institutional learning can improve policy without requiring perfect foresight at the outset.
Central rules are never useful, even when they protect minimum entitlements.
Local actors always possess complete information before implementation begins.
questions.solution: The argument depends on learning through feedback; it does not require perfect information or reject all central rules.

questions.text: Passage 1 adopts which overall rhetorical posture? Use the vending-permit register as the complete information set for this question.
options: Purely polemical and adversarial, treating competing approaches as illegitimate.
Analytical and cautious, weighing trade-offs while seeking workable improvement.
Celebratory and dismissive of risk, with little attention to implementation constraints.
Fatalistic about institutional change and doubtful that evidence can alter outcomes.
questions.solution: The wording weighs trade-offs and improvement mechanisms rather than celebrating, rejecting or attacking them.

questions.text: If r is the remainder when 7^20 + 8^18 is divided by 13, what is r? Use the ward-grievance register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Compute powers modulo 13; cyclic reduction gives remainder 2.

questions.text: How many integers from 4 through 105, inclusive, are divisible by 7 or 14, but not by both? Use the coastal-service ledger as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Count multiples of 7 and 14, then remove twice the common multiples: the exclusive count is 8.

questions.text: Solution A contains 29% solute and solution B contains 13% solute. If A and B are mixed in the volume ratio 5:1, what is the resulting concentration? Use the hill-health register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Use a weighted average: (5×29+13)/(5+1) = 26.33%.

questions.text: Three independent teams complete a task in 18, 20 and 32 days respectively. Working together at constant rates, how many days are required? Use the ration audit as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Combined rate = 1/18+1/20+1/32; reciprocal = 7.31 days.

questions.text: The average score of 25 candidates is 55. One score of 44 is replaced by 71. What is the new average? Use the tank-restoration file as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Change in average = (new−old)/25; new average = 56.08.

questions.text: A quantity rises by 17%, falls by 23%, and then rises by 29%. What is the net percentage change? Use the hostel attendance sheet as the complete information set for this question.
A rectangle of dimensions 12 m by 10 m has squares of side 2 m removed from its four corners. What area remains? Use the river-route log as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Removed area = 4×2²; remaining area = 12×10−4×2² = 104 m².

questions.text: A five-period index has values [4, 6, 8, 10, 3]; corresponding weights are [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. What is the remainder when the weighted total is divided by 17? Use the border-connectivity map as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Weighted total = 126; 126 divided by 17 leaves remainder 7.

questions.text: How many multiples of lcm(9, 10) lie in the inclusive interval [93, 367]? Use the vending-permit register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: lcm(9,10) = 90; enumerate its multiples in the interval to obtain 3.

questions.text: A sequence begins [5, 11, 16, 22]. Its successive increments are 6, 5, 6, 5, ... . What is the next term? Use the safety-inspection file as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: The increments alternate 6, 5, 6, 5; the next increment is 6, giving 33.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row. C is third from the left; A is left of D; B and F are non-adjacent; G is not at an end. Which person cannot occupy fifth position? Use the forest-response dashboard as the complete information set for this question.
options: D
C
A
B
questions.solution: Enumerating all valid arrangements gives possible fifth-position occupants ['A', 'B', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G']; C never appears there.

questions.text: Six candidates P, Q, R, S, T and U are ranked first to sixth. P is above R, R above U, S above R, Q below S, and T is not first. Which candidate cannot be third? Use the school-recovery ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: P
Q
U
R
questions.solution: Testing all rankings gives possible third-place candidates ['P', 'Q', 'R', 'S', 'T']; U violates the partial-order constraints in every valid ranking.

questions.text: In a coding rule, each letter is replaced by its position multiplied by 6, then 3 is added and the result is reduced modulo 26 (A=0). What code is assigned to the letter whose position is 7? Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.

All members of set X are in Y; no member of Y is in Z; exactly 5 members are in X, 5 additional members are in Y but not X, and 7 members are outside Y. How many members are in Y? Use the clinic-referral diary as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Y contains X plus Y-only members: 5+5 = 10.

questions.text: A field worker moves 7 km east and then 5 km north. What is the straight-line distance from the starting point, ignoring the path taken? Use the market-access survey as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Displacement = sqrt(7²+5²) = 8.60 km.

questions.text: M is the sister of N. N is the father of P. P is the daughter of Q. Relative to P, what is M? Use the ward-grievance register as the complete information set for this question.
options: P's maternal aunt
P's paternal aunt
P's paternal cousin
P's grandmother
questions.solution: N is P's father; M is N's sister, so M is P's paternal aunt.

questions.text: Exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Who is guilty? Use the coastal-service ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: B only
No one
C only
A only
questions.solution: Assume exactly one of A, B and C is guilty and exactly one statement is true. A says B is guilty; B says A and C are innocent; C says B is innocent. Testing A, B and C in turn leaves only B guilty: A and C are then false, while B is true.

questions.text: From 11 proposals, 4 are selected. Two specified proposals cannot be selected together. How many selections are possible? Use the hill-health register as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: All selections minus those containing both specified proposals: C(11,4)−C(9,2) = 294.

questions.text: A team records 5 wins, 4 draws and 1 losses. With 3 points for a win, 1 for a draw and 0 for a loss, what is its points total? Use the ration audit as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: Points = 3×5+4 = 19; losses add zero.

questions.text: A committee must choose an ordered pair of distinct coordinators from 6 eligible members. How many ordered pairs are possible? Use the tank-restoration file as the complete information set for this question.
questions.solution: The first post has 6 choices and the second has 5; ordered pairs therefore total 6×5 = 30.

questions.text: In a coastal district, a file concerning cyclone shelter access is being reviewed by ward officers; the available evidence includes travel-time logs. A pilot produces mixed results across neighbourhoods. How should the administrator respond? Use the hostel attendance sheet as the complete information set for this question.
options: Hide the mixed results until a later evaluation produces a simpler narrative.
Examine context-specific results, adapt the design and publish the decision rule.
Scale it everywhere immediately because any positive result proves universal effectiveness.
Cancel it everywhere immediately because variation means the intervention has failed.
questions.solution: Disaggregated evidence supports adaptation rather than premature scaling, cancellation or concealment.

questions.text: In a coastal district, a file concerning cyclone shelter access is being reviewed by ward officers; the available evidence includes travel-time logs. A grievance channel receives fewer complaints after a redesign. What is the most careful interpretation? Use the river-route log as the complete information set for this question.
options: Stop monitoring because the lower number already provides a sufficient success signal.
Conclude that the redesign failed because every effective channel should receive more complaints.
Check accessibility, repeat-use patterns and independent feedback before judging the change.
Conclude that service quality improved because fewer complaints always mean fewer problems.
questions.solution: Complaint counts need accessibility and independent-feedback checks before they can indicate improvement.

questions.text: In a coastal district, a file concerning cyclone shelter access is being reviewed by ward officers; the available evidence includes travel-time logs. A contractor asks to relax a safety condition to meet a deadline. What should the officer do? Use the border-connectivity map as the complete information set for this question.
options: Reject every modification without examining whether an equivalent safeguard is available.
Approve the relaxation because schedule performance is the most visible project outcome.
Ask the contractor to proceed informally so that the paperwork does not delay work.
Assess the risk, apply the documented change-control rule and retain a safe alternative.
questions.solution: A documented risk and change-control assessment protects safety without making procedure an empty ritual.

questions.text: In a coastal district, a file concerning cyclone shelter access is being reviewed by ward officers; the available evidence includes travel-time logs. A beneficiary list contains duplicate names and some genuine exclusions. What is the right sequence? Use the vending-permit register as the complete information set for this question.
options: Add every claimant immediately and leave verification to a later unrecorded exercise.
Deduplicate transparently, publish an appeal window and verify excluded claims.
Freeze enrolment indefinitely because cleaning the list may create further disputes.
Delete all duplicate-looking names first and accept the resulting list as final.
questions.solution: Transparent deduplication plus appeal and verification addresses both leakage and wrongful exclusion.

questions.text: In a coastal district, a file concerning cyclone shelter access is being reviewed by ward officers; the available evidence includes travel-time logs. A local leader requests an exception for one influential applicant. What is defensible? Use the safety-inspection file as the complete information set for this question.
options: Grant the exception because the applicant's influence may speed wider cooperation.
Ask the leader to obtain informal consent from staff before changing the record.
Deny every request without checking whether a general hardship rule already exists.
Apply the published hardship criteria equally and document any exceptional decision.
questions.solution: Equal application of a published rule protects fairness while allowing genuinely defined hardship relief.

questions.text: In a hill block, a file concerning primary-health referrals is being reviewed by clinic managers; the available evidence includes referral registers. A new digital process excludes some intended users. What should the officer do first? Use the forest-response dashboard as the complete information set for this question.
options: Require universal digital use so that one procedure applies to every applicant.
Ask users to arrange private help while leaving the official process unchanged.
Cancel the process and restore the former manual arrangement for every applicant.
Retain the process, add assisted access and an auditable fallback, then review evidence.
questions.solution: The response preserves useful innovation while removing exclusion through assisted access, fallback and review.

questions.text: In a hill block, a file concerning primary-health referrals is being reviewed by clinic managers; the available evidence includes referral registers. Two agencies submit conflicting records before a time-sensitive public intervention. What is the soundest next step? Use the school-recovery ledger as the complete information set for this question.
options: Choose the record from the agency with the larger budget and proceed immediately.
Postpone the intervention indefinitely until the agencies reach an informal agreement.
Publish both records as equally reliable and begin implementation without reconciliation.
Create a shared evidence set, record assumptions and commission a rapid joint verification.
questions.solution: A shared evidence base and explicit assumptions address disagreement without arbitrary choice or paralysis.

questions.text: In a hill block, a file concerning primary-health referrals is being reviewed by clinic managers; the available evidence includes referral registers. A service reports high activity, but users say their underlying problems remain unresolved. Which measure should follow? Use the municipal works map as the complete information set for this question.
options: Count publicity material and attendance figures because visibility indicates institutional effort.
Track average interaction time without separating issues or checking final outcomes.
Count total interactions without classification so that the headline number remains comparable.
Track resolution by issue type and verify a sample through independent follow-up calls.
questions.solution: Outcome-by-issue plus verified follow-up distinguishes visible activity from effective service delivery.

questions.text: In a hill block, a file concerning primary-health referrals is being reviewed by clinic managers; the available evidence includes referral registers. A fund can support a visible ceremony or a tested low-cost intervention. Which decision is stronger? Use the clinic-referral diary as the complete information set for this question.
options: Choose the tested intervention, publish the baseline and specify a review point.
Choose the visible event because all stakeholders can observe its immediate completion.
Choose neither option until the underlying problem disappears without further intervention.
Divide funds equally even if neither activity then has enough resources to operate.
questions.solution: The evidence-supported intervention creates an accountable learning loop and a reviewable use of funds.

questions.text: In a hill block, a file concerning primary-health referrals is being reviewed by clinic managers; the available evidence includes referral registers. A lowest bid has a minor clerical error but no evidence of material advantage. What is fairest? Use the market-access survey as the complete information set for this question.
options: Ignore the error silently so that the procurement record remains uncomplicated.
Apply the published correction rule consistently and record the reasons for the decision.
Reject the bid automatically because any clerical error establishes bad faith.
Invite the bidder to alter unrelated parts of the submission before evaluation continues.
questions.solution: Consistent use of a pre-published rule protects equal treatment, transparency and auditability.
